response:
It is incredibly painful to pour years of sacrifice into raising your children, only to feel unappreciated and watch them gravitate toward a parent who caused you harm. Your feelings of deep hurt are completely valid. Often, young adults do not fully grasp the complexities of their parents' past, especially if they were shielded from the abuse or if the other parent presents a different version of themselves today. 

While you cannot control their relationship with their father, you can protect your own peace. It is okay to set firm boundaries with your youngest daughter, calmly letting her know that calling you "crazy" is disrespectful and unacceptable. Because this situation brings up the trauma of your past abuse and the grief of feeling unseen, speaking with a counselor could be very helpful. A professional can help you navigate these complex dynamics and find ways to heal while focusing on the happiness you have built in your new marriage.
